BEGINNING OF CONVERSATION: USER: Why is the northern hemisphere winter solstice in December, but late January and early February are always the coldest times of the year? ASSISTANT:

The northern hemisphere winter solstice occurs in December because the Earth's axis is tilted away from the sun, resulting in less direct sunlight reaching the northern hemisphere at this time of year. This causes the days to be shorter and the nights to be longer, resulting in colder temperatures. However, late January and early February are typically the coldest times of the year because the atmosphere is at its most stable, allowing cold air to settle and remain at the surface.
